key_insight: SkillFuzz treats skill composition as a fuzzing problem, exposing hidden “implicit intents” that only appear when individually safe skills interact inside an LLM agent.
engineering_relevance: It helps marketplace operators and agent builders screen skill bundles before deployment, reducing the risk of unintended agent behavior without needing execution-time environments.
method: Use contract-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search to prioritize risky compositions.
Compare planning artifacts against a skill-free baseline as a differential oracle.
evidence_signal: On representative workloads, SkillFuzz found over 1,000 distinct implicit intents under a fixed query budget and confirmed more than 80% of the highest-risk flagged compositions during execution-time validation.
watch_item: Results depend on the quality of extracted skill contracts and planning artifacts, so incomplete skill descriptions or atypical agent planners may reduce detection accuracy.
paper_title: SkillFuzz: Fuzzing Skill Composition for Implicit Intents Discovery in Open Skill Marketplaces
